false_positives.candidate:
Strategy close() shuts down the factory-shared queue pool, so later strategies drop and commit messages
The FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared by every strategy that create_with_partitions builds. Arroyo closes the strategy on every rebalance or partition revocation, and close() calls queue_pool.shutdown(). That stops all workers and shuts down all queues. The next strategy created after the rebalance reuses the dead pool. FixedQueuePool.submit calls work_queue.put, which raises queue.ShutDown. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches it, marks the offset complete, and the commit loop then commits it. Every message is silently dropped and its offset advanced. The OffsetTracker also keeps stale last_committed and all_offsets from the old assignment across rebalances.

Unbounded queues give no backpressure despite the documented guarantee
The class docstring promises natural backpressure when queues fill up. The queues are created with queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and poll() never pauses or rejects. If processing is slower than consumption, for example a slow DB, the consumer keeps reading and buffering messages. Memory grows without bound, and a crash then reprocesses everything.

Commit is invoked from a background thread, and pending offsets are not flushed on close
Arroyo's commit callable is designed to be called from the consumer thread, and the strategy calls it from its own thread instead. close() sets the shutdown event, and the loop exits without a final commit of already-completed offsets. After a revoke, the loop can also still call commit for partitions that are no longer assigned.
